_note: Renée owns every sentence here. Claude drafted the first pass August 2026 — edit freely. A slot left empty renders nothing at all. Placeholders {ships}, {pax}, {month} and {time} are filled in automatically.

slots.TRAFFIC_EMPTY: About as quiet as this island gets. Empty roads, empty beaches.
slots.TRAFFIC_QUIET: Quiet day. Roads are clear and you can get anywhere without thinking about it.
slots.TRAFFIC_BUSY: Philipsburg busy, Maho gets the overflow, roads otherwise fine.
slots.TRAFFIC_CONGESTED: Philipsburg and Maho will be packed and the roads slow until about four. Expect heavy traffic across the island.
slots.TRAFFIC_GRIDLOCK: The port is at capacity. Crossing the island between ten and four is going to hurt.
slots.TRAFFIC_ZERO_SHIPS_STILL_BUSY: No ships today, but the island is full anyway. The flights fill it just as much.
slots.TRAFFIC_DATA_STALE: We do not have today's port schedule, so assume the usual.
slots.ANOMALY_EXCEPTIONAL: This is not what {month} normally looks like.
slots.BRIDGE_UPCOMING: Simpson Bay Bridge is due to open at {time}. Nothing happens if no boat turns up, but Welfare Road may stop for fifteen minutes.
slots.SWELL_NORTH_WEST_ROUGH: North swell is running. Baie Rouge, Plum Bay, Mullet Bay and Cupecoy have shore break and rips today — Great Bay, Little Bay and Le Galion stay flat.
slots.SWELL_EAST_CHOPPY: Trades are up and the Atlantic side is choppy — Orient Bay, Dawn Beach and Guana Bay. Le Galion and Coconut Grove stay flat behind the reef.
slots.SWELL_CALM: Flat calm islandwide — even Orient Bay and Dawn Beach are gentle today.
slots.SARGASSUM_LIKELY: Sargassum season — the Atlantic-facing beaches (Orient, Le Galion, Dawn, Coconut Grove) are the ones to check before you drive out.
slots.SARGASSUM_POSSIBLE: Edge of sargassum season — the Atlantic-facing beaches are the ones worth checking before you drive out.
slots.SARGASSUM_UNLIKELY: Sargassum season is over. The east side is clear.
slots.CROWD_AVOID_LIST: Maho, Mullet, Orient and the Boardwalk will be shoulder to shoulder until about four.
slots.CROWD_ESCAPE_LIST: Happy Bay, Baie Rouge, Plum and Friar's stay quiet on ship days.
slots.EVENT_FRENCH_CARNIVAL: Carnival in Marigot. Road closures, parades, and no parking anywhere near town.
slots.EVENT_DUTCH_CARNIVAL: Carnival season on the Dutch side. Philipsburg has parades and the roads around them shut down.
slots.EVENT_REGATTA: Heineken Regatta week. Simpson Bay is full of boats and the bars are three deep.
slots.EVENT_PUBLIC_HOLIDAY_DUTCH: Dutch-side holiday. Philipsburg and Simpson Bay will be mostly shut.
slots.EVENT_PUBLIC_HOLIDAY_FRENCH: French-side holiday. Grand Case and Marigot will be mostly shut.
slots.CLOSURE_SEPTEMBER: Low season, so a good part of the French side is closed for the year. Call before you drive to Grand Case.
slots.SPECIALS_LOW_SEASON_CAVEAT: Low season, so call ahead. Most of the French side shuts from late August to mid-October.
slots.BRIDGE_SIMPSON_BAY: Simpson Bay Bridge is due to open at {time}. Welfare Road through the village stops for about fifteen minutes — if you are heading to Cole Bay or Philipsburg, be past the Yacht Club before then.
slots.BRIDGE_SANDY_GROUND: Sandy Ground Bridge is due to open at {time}. That is the only road from Marigot out to Baie Nettlé and Terres Basses, and there is no short way round, so wait it out.
slots.BRIDGE_BOTH_0830: Simpson Bay Bridge and Sandy Ground Bridge are both due at 8:30, in the middle of the morning rush. Welfare Road and the Marigot sandbar road stop at the same time.
slots.BRIDGE_BOTH_1700: Worst window of the day. Simpson Bay Bridge and Sandy Ground Bridge are both due at 5:00, right as the ships leave and everyone drives home. If you have a flight, be east of Cole Bay by 4:45.
slots.SWELL_NORTH_WEST_DANGEROUS: Dangerous shore break at Baie Rouge, Plum Bay, Mullet Bay and Cupecoy — waves dumping onto a steep slope and dragging people back out. There are no lifeguards anywhere on this island. Swim at Great Bay or Le Galion today.
slots.SWELL_EAST_WINDY: Wind is over twenty knots. Orient Bay and Dawn Beach will be blown sand and flying umbrellas — go to Little Bay or Friar's Bay for shelter, or to Le Galion if you would rather kitesurf than sunbathe.
